title: v1.19.0 re-issues certificates unnecessarily — go straight to a later 1.19 patch

detection.reason: the add-on version is resolved to a MINOR from the controller image tag, so no rule can compare patch levels

quote: When upgrading to cert-manager `1.19`, use the latest patch version of cert-manager `1.19`. Do not install `v1.19.0`, because it has a bug which may cause certificates to be re-issued unnecessarily. We fixed the bug in `v1.19.1`.
remediation: Upgrade to the newest 1.19 patch. Never to v1.19.0: it re-issues certificates unnecessarily, which for an ACME issuer can mean hitting rate limits.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.template.spec.containers[] | select(.image | test("cert-manager-controller")) | .image'  # the tag printed must not be v1.19.0

title: The ACME client metrics lose their path label — dashboards and alerts on it go blank

detection.reason: PrometheusRule and Grafana dashboards are not collected, and a recording rule or dashboard living outside the cluster cannot be seen at all

quote: A high cardinality label, called `path`, was removed from the `certmanager_acme_client_request_count` and `certmanager_acme_client_request_duration_seconds` metrics. It is replaced with a new bounded cardinality label called `action`. If you are using these metrics, you may need to update your dashboards and alerts.
remediation: Update any dashboard or alert selecting on the `path` label of `certmanager_acme_client_request_count` or `certmanager_acme_client_request_duration_seconds` to the bounded `action` label before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get prometheusrules -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec | tostring | test("certmanager_acme_client_request")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row references these metrics; anything selecting on `path` matches nothing after 1.19

title: cert-manager-edit no longer lets namespace users create Challenges or Orders

detection.reason: the agent projects only the pod-subresource rules of a ClusterRole, so which API groups cert-manager-edit grants cannot be read; and tooling that creates Challenge or Order objects directly may not live on this cluster at all

quote: Starting in v1.19.6, the `cert-manager-edit` aggregate ClusterRole no longer grants `create` for `challenges.acme.cert-manager.io` or `create`, `patch`, `update` for `orders.acme.cert-manager.io`. This fixes a security issue (`GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258`) where these permissions allowed namespace users to bypass Issuer solver selectors and abuse ClusterIssuer credentials.
remediation: If any tooling creates Challenge or Order resources directly — outside the normal Certificate → CertificateRequest → Order → Challenge flow — grant it those permissions explicitly. This closed a security issue (GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258) and is not being reverted.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterrole cert-manager-edit -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.rules[] | select(.apiGroups[]? | test("acme.cert-manager.io")) | "\(.resources | join(",")): \(.verbs | join(","))"'  # create on challenges, and create/patch/update on orders, are what the upgrade removes
coversNotes: Restrict Challenge and Order RBAC in `cert-manager-edit` ClusterRole
